title: Scaling a Database
subtitle: Reads scale out; writes need to be split
motto: Replicas cure read pain and do nothing for writes
keyInsight: Replicas scale reads but every write still goes to one primary, so scaling writes means splitting the data, at the price of cross-shard queries.

decisions.title: Grow writes, not reads, in the failure frame
decisions.description: Replicas already fixed the read load, so the failure quadruples writes to show exactly the case replicas cannot help.
decisions.alternatives: Growing both together would blur which fix addresses which problem.

decisions.title: Make replication lag depend on primary load
decisions.description: Lag rises as the primary gets busier and hits a ceiling when it saturates, so the consistency cost of replicas is visible.
decisions.alternatives: A fixed lag figure is simpler but would not show that overloading the primary makes replicas fall further behind.
